# entr - Event Notify Test Runner

A utility for running arbitrary commands when files change. `entr` watches files and executes commands when they are modified.

## Description

`entr` reads a list of files from standard input and executes a specified command when any of those files change. It provides a fast, efficient way to get rapid feedback during development.

## Usage

```
entr [-acdnprsxz] utility [argument /_ ...]
```

## Options

- `-a` - Respond to all events which occur while the utility is running
- `-c` - Clear the screen before invoking the utility (specify twice to erase scrollback)
- `-d` - Track the parent directory of files. Specify twice to recognize all new directory entries
- `-n` - Run in non-interactive mode
- `-p` - Postpone the first execution until a file is modified
- `-r` - Reload a persistent child process
- `-s` - Evaluate the first argument using the SHELL environment variable
- `-x` - Format custom exit status messages using awk
- `-z` - Exit after the utility completes

## Special Features

- The argument `/_` is replaced with the absolute path of the first file to trigger an event
- Press `space` to manually execute the utility
- Press `q` to quit

## Environment Variables

- `ENTR_STATUS_SCRIPT` - Path to exit status script (default: `$HOME/.entr/status.awk`)
- `ENTR_RESTART_SIGNAL` - Signal used to terminate the utility (HUP, INT, QUIT, TERM, USR1, USR2)
- `ENTR_INOTIFY_WORKAROUND` - Enable for incomplete inotify support (WSL, Docker for Mac)
- `ENTR_FOLLOW_SYMLINK` - Follow symlinks (Mac OS and Linux)
- `EV_TRACE` - Print file system event messages
- `SHELL` - Specify shell for `-s` flag (default: `/bin/sh`)
- `PAGER` - Default set to `/bin/cat`

## Examples

Rebuild a project if source files change, limiting output to the first 20 lines:

```bash
$ find src/ | entr -s 'make | head -n 20'
```

Launch and auto-reload a node.js server:

```bash
$ ls *.js | entr -r node app.js
```

Clear the screen and run a query after the SQL script is updated:

```bash
$ echo my.sql | entr -cp psql -f /_
```

Rebuild project if a source file is modified or added to the src/ directory:

```bash
$ while sleep 0.1; do ls -d src src/*.rb | entr -d make; done
```

Auto-reload a web server, or terminate if the server exits:

```bash
$ ls * | entr -rz ./httpd
```

## Exit Status

When `-z` flag is set, returns the exit status of the child process.

Otherwise:
- `0` - Normal termination after receiving SIGINT
- `1` - No regular files provided or error occurred
- `2` - Files were added or removed from a directory

## Interactive Commands

While entr is running:
- `space` - Execute the utility immediately
- `q` - Quit

## Platform Support

Supported on BSD, Mac OS, and Linux systems. On Mac OS and Linux, symlinks are not followed unless `ENTR_FOLLOW_SYMLINK` is set.

For environments with incomplete inotify support (Windows Subsystem for Linux, Docker for Mac), set `ENTR_INOTIFY_WORKAROUND` to enable proper operation.

.Bl -tag -width <space>
.It Aq Cm space
Execute the utility immediately.
If the
.Fl Cm r
option is set this will terminate and restart the child process as if a file
change event had occurred.
.It Cm q
Quit; equivalent pressing
.Aq Cm control-C .
.El
.Sh ENVIRONMENT
.Bl -tag -width "ENTR_ENVIRON"
.It Ev ENTR_STATUS_SCRIPT
The path to the exit status script enabled by the
.Fl x
option.
By default
.Pa $HOME/.entr/status.awk
is evaluated.
.It Ev ENTR_RESTART_SIGNAL
Signal used to terminate the
.Ar utility .
Supported signal names are
.Dv HUP ,
.Dv INT ,
.Dv QUIT ,
.Dv TERM ,
.Dv USR1
and
.Dv USR2 .
The default is
.Dv SIGTERM .
.It Ev EV_TRACE
Print file system event messages.
.It Ev PAGER
Set to
.Pa /bin/cat
by default
to prevent interactive utilities from waiting for keyboard input if output does
not fit on the screen.
.It Ev SHELL
Specify the shell to use with the
.Fl s
flag.
The default is
.Pa /bin/sh .
.El
.Sh EXIT STATUS
If the
.Fl z
flag is set and the
.Ar utility
is successfully executed, the status of the child process is returned.
If the child process was terminated by a signal, the exit status is the signal
number plus 128.
.Pp
.Nm
normally returns one of the following values:
.Pp
.Bl -tag -width Ds -offset indent -compact
.It 0
Normal termination after receiving
.Dv SIGINT
.It 1
No regular files were provided as input or an error occurred
.It 2
Files were added or removed from a directory
.El
.Sh EXAMPLES
Rebuild a project if source files change, limiting output to the first 20 lines:
.Pp
.Dl $ find src/ | entr -s 'make | head -n 20'
.Pp
Launch and auto-reload a node.js server:
.Pp
.Dl $ ls *.js | entr -r node app.js
.Pp
Clear the screen and run a query after the SQL script is updated:
.Pp
.Dl $ echo my.sql | entr -cp psql -f /_
.Pp
Rebuild project if a source file is modified or added to the src/ directory:
.Pp
.Dl $ while sleep 0.1; do ls -d src src/*.rb | entr make; done
.Pp

.Pp
.Dl $ ls * | entr -rz ./httpd

import subprocess, os, time, signal, sys
ENTR="/workspace/executable"
def start(args, files, cwd="/tmp/entrtest", env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    if env: e.update(env)
    # ensure files reset?
    p=subprocess.Popen([ENTR]+args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, cwd=cwd, env=e, text=True, bufsize=1)
    p.stdin.write("".join(f+"\n" for f in files))
    p.stdin.close()
    return p

def readavail(p, dur=0.8):
    import select
    out=[]
    # Use select on stdout/stderr separately? simplistic: set nonblocking via os
    import fcntl
    for name, f in [("out",p.stdout),("err",p.stderr)]:
        fd=f.fileno()
        flags=fcntl.fcntl(fd, fcntl.F_GETFL)
        fcntl.fcntl(fd, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags|os.O_NONBLOCK)
        end=time.time()+dur
        data=b""
        # just try read
        try:
            chunk=os.read(fd, 65536)
            data+=chunk
        except BlockingIOError:
            pass
        fcntl.fcntl(fd, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags)
        if data:
            out.append((name,data))
    return out

def wait_output(p, dur=2, poll=0.05):
    # read until timeout using select
    import select
    outputs={"out":b"","err":b""}
    fds={p.stdout.fileno():"out", p.stderr.fileno():"err"}
    end=time.time()+dur
    while time.time()<end:
        r,_,_=select.select(list(fds.keys()),[],[],0.1)
        if not r:
            # if we already have some data maybe break? caller decides
            if outputs["out"] or outputs["err"]:
                # wait a bit more?
                pass
            continue
        for fd in r:
            try:
                data=os.read(fd,65536)
            except OSError:
                data=b""
            if data:
                outputs[fds[fd]]+=data
        # if short...
    return outputs

def drain(p, dur=0.6):
    import select
    outputs={"out":b"","err":b""}
    fds={p.stdout.fileno():"out", p.stderr.fileno():"err"}
    end=time.time()+dur
    while time.time()<end:
        timeout=max(0,end-time.time())
        r,_,_=select.select(list(fds.keys()),[],[],timeout)
        if not r:
            break
        for fd in r:
            data=os.read(fd,65536)
            if data:
                outputs[fds[fd]]+=data
    return outputs

def touch(path, content=None):
    if content is None:
        # modify by appending? Or rewrite
        with open(path,"a") as f: f.write("x")
    else:
        with open(path,"w") as f: f.write(content)

open("/tmp/entrtest/a.txt","w").write("A\n")

def run_case(name, use_stdout_tty=False, use_stderr_tty=False, set_ctty=False, stdin_tty=False):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    slave_name=os.ttyname(slave)
    def setup_ctty():
        os.setsid()
        fd=os.open(slave_name, os.O_RDWR)
        fcntl.ioctl(fd, 0x540E, 0)
    def setup_noctty():
        os.setsid()
    stdout_dest = slave if use_stdout_tty else subprocess.PIPE
    stderr_dest = slave if use_stderr_tty else subprocess.PIPE
    stdin_dest = slave if stdin_tty else subprocess.PIPE
    p=subprocess.Popen(["/workspace/executable","echo","EV"], stdin=stdin_dest, stdout=stdout_dest, stderr=stderr_dest, cwd="/tmp/entrtest", preexec_fn=(setup_ctty if set_ctty else setup_noctty), text=True)
    if not stdin_tty:
        p.stdin.write("a.txt\n"); p.stdin.close()
    else:
        # send file list into master, then EOF char? Ctrl-D
        os.write(master,b"a.txt\n")
        os.write(master,b"\x04")
    time.sleep(0.8)
    # read pipes if avail
    out=b""
    if not use_stdout_tty:
        print(name, "drain pipes", drain(p,0.8), "poll", p.poll())

        # read master
        import select
        data=b""
        while True:
            r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.5)
            if not r: break
            try: chunk=os.read(master,65536)
            except OSError: break
            if not chunk: break
            data+=chunk

    try: print("  wait",p.wait(timeout=2))

    os.close(master); os.close(slave)

import os, pty, subprocess, signal, time, sys, termios, fcntl, select
os.chdir("/tmp/entrtest")
open("/tmp/entrtest/a.txt","w").write("A\n")
master, slave = pty.openpty()
def setup():
    os.setsid()
    fcntl.ioctl(0,0x540E,0)
# all std fds slave
p=subprocess.Popen(["/workspace/executable","echo","EV"], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd="/tmp/entrtest", preexec_fn=setup, close_fds=True)
os.close(slave)
time.sleep(0.5)
def readm(dur=0.7):
    data=b""; end=time.time()+dur
    while time.time()<end:
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],max(0,end-time.time()))
        if not r: break
        try: c=os.read(master,65536)
        except Exception as e: print("read err",e); break
        if not c: break
        data+=c
    return data
print("initial master", readm())
print("poll",p.poll())
# send filenames then Ctrl-D?
os.write(master,b"a.txt\n")
print("after filename", readm())
os.write(master,b"\x04")
print("after ctrl-d", readm(1.5))
print("poll",p.poll())
# now entr should be running, initial EV output expected if it runs
os.write(master,b"q")
print("after q",readm())
print("poll/wait",p.poll(), (p.wait(timeout=2) if p.poll() is not None else "alive"))
if p.poll() is None: p.kill(); p.wait()
